topic: Type Qualifiers and cv-Qualification in Pointer-to-Member Types
explanation: In C++, pointer-to-member types can include cv-qualifiers (const and volatile) that specify the qualification of the member being pointed to. When combining multiple pointer-to-member types, especially in contexts involving inheritance or reference-related classes, the cv-qualifiers are merged according to specific rules to produce a cv-qualified type that accurately reflects the combined qualifications. This mechanism ensures type safety and correctness when working with member pointers across class hierarchies, enabling precise control over constness and volatility in object-oriented programming.
syntax:
pointer-to-member type: cv-qualification class_name::member_type
cv-qualification merging: cv-combined type of T1 and T2 is determined by combining their cv-qualifiers according to rules in 8.5.3 of the standard, considering class inheritance relationships.
example_explanation: This example illustrates how pointer-to-member types can include cv-qualifiers such as const and volatile. It shows the declaration of pointers to members of classes with different cv-qualifiers and hints at how, when combining such types—especially across class hierarchies—the cv-qualifiers are merged according to the rules specified in the standard. This ensures that the resulting pointer-to-member type accurately reflects the combined constness or volatility, maintaining type safety in object-oriented C++ programming.
